releases.name: Q-Pathformer Study v0.9 — Learned Routing and Classical Controls
releases.body:
# Q-Pathformer Study v0.9 — Learned Routing and Classical Controls

Prepared for owner review as a GitHub draft. Repository edition v1.0 is separate from study v0.9.

Learned circuit routing won five, lost three and was inconclusive in four of twelve primary BCE contrasts; three wins exceeded the 0.01 practical reference throughout their adjusted intervals. G121 remained much better on checkerboard and spiral. MLP4 led the descriptive Banknote check. Exact conversion preserved 276 circuit predictors and 1,380 expert cores.

Plan B compares hard geometric routing, fixed soft mixtures, learned soft mixtures, parameter-count-matched residual controls and G121. Four synthetic families use eight confirmation populations and two paired optimizer seeds. Banknote Authentication is a secondary fixed grouped split with five optimizer seeds and additional MLP2, MLP4 and LR2 controls.

48 engineering, 72 development, 636 confirmation and four clean retraining fits. Banknote is one fixed split, not five independent datasets. Shared diagnostic numerical primitives, small-sample t assumptions, mixture costs, local timing and absent physical hardware constrain claims. The original top-level READ_ME.txt is a stale preparation notice; final report and acceptance records govern completion.

The Study, Documentation and Code ZIPs each have a matching external integrity seal. The report preserves every original paragraph, table and embedded figure, with a disclosed edition note and corrected metadata. Original source code is unchanged.

The owner adopted the same scoped licenses as v0.1 and v0.9.5: CC BY 4.0 for controlled original report and listed explanatory prose, and unchanged Q-Pathformer Platform License 1.0 for exact selected Python. Earlier permissions remain in force. Third-party material, datasets, model artifacts, architecture documents and full archives retain separate terms.

Fresh extraction, inventories, checksums and bounded offline startup passed. No full training, official scoring, shot sampling or physical hardware jobs were run. Full reproduction requires excluded source data, checkpoints and reviewed historical environment/path bindings. Retained full-archive logical payload size is 34,582,760,206 bytes; it is not a download size or hardware minimum.

# Q-Pathformer Study v0.8 — Priority Training and Routed Models

Prepared for owner review as a GitHub draft. Repository edition v1.0 is separate from study v0.8.

Priority improved four of eight direct registered BCE comparisons, with the other four inconclusive; none established more than 0.01 BCE improvement across the entire interval. Priority did not close the routed circuit gap to the wider global baseline on checkerboard or spiral. Exact conversion preserved predictions (maximum probability difference below 2.62e-14) and improved local latency.

40 engineering, 80 development and 640 confirmation fits, plus four preselected clean retrains. All 20 primary comparisons are retained. Reproduction fits are not new independent populations. Three timing sessions varied; retained source reports preserve these limits. No physical quantum or new finite-shot campaign is claimed.

# Q-Pathformer Study v0.7 — Routing Capacity and Classical Deployment

Prepared for owner review as a GitHub draft. Repository edition v1.0 is separate from study v0.7.

Geometric routing consistently outperformed matched-count hash routing. The global Trig121 control led the two harder clean tasks (98.47% checkerboard and 96.57% spiral macro-F1 versus 76.57% and 86.82% for the flexible circuit). Classical compilation preserved checked class predictions and accelerated single-input circuit calls 4.28–4.58 times. These historical measurements do not establish quantum advantage.

Eight arms compare scalar and flexible routed two-qubit circuit emulation, geometric and matched-count hash routing, routed/global trigonometric controls and an MLP on checkerboard, spiral, noisy annulus and rare disks. Confirmation uses eight independent populations per task and two paired optimizer seeds per population.

608 registered fits, including 512 confirmation endpoints; 20 primary paired population-level BCE contrasts. Small-sample interval assumptions, four synthetic families and host-specific timing limit generalization. Finite-shot sensitivity was historical local simulation, not physical hardware.

releases.name: Q-Pathformer Study v0.6 — Harder Tasks and Faster Inference
releases.body:
# Q-Pathformer Study v0.6 — Harder Tasks and Faster Inference

Six registered models compare scalar and multiple-moment circuit readouts with routed and global classical controls on checkerboard, spiral, noisy-annulus and rare-positive-disk families. The richer readout improves the difficult clean-boundary tasks; the routed trigonometric control remains stronger there. Exact classical coefficient conversion accelerates the same trained circuits without changing their decisions; it is not another efficacy arm. The study completed 48 development and 120 confirmation endpoints, plus 24 engineering endpoints.

Three curated downloads provide the preserved report in PDF and Word, guidance and selected code. Each ZIP has an external integrity seal. Full retained evidence is excluded. Anthony Siljeg adopted the same separately scoped report/prose and Python scheme as v0.1 and v0.9.5; applicable earlier grants remain unchanged.

The results concern small two-dimensional synthetic classifiers on classical CPU hardware. Five paired seeds and one split per family do not establish population-wide or real-world generalization. Historical prior-version scores are context, not paired evidence of improvement. Local compilation, noise and shot results are simulator evidence, with no physical-QPU result or quantum-advantage claim. The full proposed language architecture was not benchmarked.

Prepared as a private draft release for owner review. No new scientific experiment or full reproduction is claimed.

Eleven small model recipes compare flexible circuit readouts with neural-network and trigonometric controls on fresh two-dimensional circle and ellipse tasks. Learned scalar and five-moment readouts improve on the legacy output, while strong trigonometric controls retain the most attractive accuracy and cost combination. releases.name: Q-Pathformer Study v0.4 — Routing and Circuit Contribution
releases.body:
# Q-Pathformer Study v0.4 — Routing and Circuit Contribution

**Draft release for owner review.** Repository edition v1.0 is separate from study v0.4.

Nine combinations of model family and routing were evaluated: two-qubit depth-two circuits, raw-input ReLU MLPs and 25-feature trigonometric logit models, each with global, coordinate-hash or train-only k-means routing. All 54 development and 135 confirmation endpoints completed 200 rounds and 15000 optimizer updates. Confirmation covered two independent circle populations and a rotated ellipse.

Q2 k-means mean macro-F1 was 98.32%, 97.16% and 94.41% across the three confirmation populations. Spatial routing substantially improved Q2 relative to hash routing, but trigonometric k-means models had lower BCE throughout. Global MLP and trigonometric controls also outperformed Q2 k-means in mean F1 and BCE. Q2 versus the small routed MLP was unresolved across training seeds.

Five seeds, synthetic tasks, fixed routers and unequal capacities do not isolate a circuit-specific benefit or establish quantum advantage, equivalence, speed or real-world generalization. Seed intervals and conditional record bootstraps answer different questions. Local readiness covered 45 quantum checkpoints, 1440 validation fixture circuits and 720 measured Aer experiments totaling 737280 simulated shots; 199065600 represented binomial trials are separate. Illustrative noise is not device calibration.

releases.name: Q-Pathformer Study v0.3 — Shallow Circuits and Routing
releases.body:
# Q-Pathformer Study v0.3 — Shallow Circuits and Routing

**Draft release for owner review.** Repository edition v1.0 is separate from study v0.3.

All 104 registered training runs completed: 39 development and 65 confirmation. Thirteen methods continued to five-seed confirmation on fresh synthetic circle data. Independent replay checked 65 endpoints, 104000 predictions and 150 saved shot arrays.

Confirmation mean macro-F1 was 97.42% for k-means routed depth-two circuits, 90.10% for hash routing with the same 40 circuit angles, 94.06% for a fixed depth-four circuit and 98.70% for the larger classical MLP. Routing improved the circuit model, while the spatial partition also added classical capacity.

One synthetic task and five confirmation training seeds do not establish quantum advantage or real-domain generalization. A development numerical-threshold failure and a verification-only pre-confirmation amendment are preserved in the historical evidence. Confirmation had zero ambiguous predictions. Local Aer checks used 150 circuits and 3840000 simulated measurement shots; separate probability-level binomial analysis is not hardware execution or device-noise simulation.

releases.name: Q-Pathformer Study v0.2 — Improvement Study and Baseline Comparison
releases.body:
**Draft for owner review · Private repository · Study · Documentation · Code**

Q-Pathformer v0.2 tested two design questions: whether stable text routing improves classification, and whether separate parameter banks improve small circuits that operate at different depths. This completed study is presented in **Q-Pathformer Classical Research, repository edition v1.0**; the repository edition and study version are separate identifiers.

The work combines a classical GPU text experiment on **DBpedia14 title-plus-content classification** with a separate synthetic circuit experiment. All **94 registered main runs** (27 text and 67 circuit-study runs) and **eight separate common text warmups** completed. Confirmation covered 15 text endpoints and 40 circuit-study endpoints, including classical controls in the latter.

### Main findings

**Text routing:** Hash18 reached **97.659% macro-F1**, compared with **97.642%** for current content routing and **97.602%** for shared adapters. Its primary mean gain over current content routing was **0.01694 percentage points**, with paired seed t95 interval **[-0.11024, +0.14412]**. The interval includes zero; the study did not establish a resolved primary improvement.

**Circuit parameters:** Giving each depth its own parameter bank improved the selected comparison with the original shared-parameter schedule. Untied assigned circuits reached **81.44% macro-F1**, compared with **71.83%** for the shared schedule. The change increased allocated angles from **16 to 40**. The fixed four-layer circuit reached **93.32%**, and the matched-information classical **MLP129 reached 99.04%**. The primary circuit comparison used binary cross-entropy: untied assigned minus shared schedule was **-0.14441**, with paired seed t95 interval **[-0.15434, -0.13449]**; lower is better. F1 is secondary.

The text experiment used a classical GPU; the quantum circuits were simulated locally. No physical-QPU execution or quantum advantage is reported. These are separate models on separate tasks, not an integrated quantum text model. The parameter-bank comparison does not isolate a scheduling or gradient-interference benefit, and MLP129 is information-matched rather than parameter- or compute-matched.

### Downloads

| Download | Contents | External seal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `QPathformer_v0.2_Study.zip` | Preserved PDF and Word report, report rights and provenance | `QPathformer_v0.2_Study.seal.json` |
| `QPathformer_v0.2_Documentation.zip` | Research guide, findings, reproduction boundaries and historical guidance | `QPathformer_v0.2_Documentation.seal.json` |
| `QPathformer_v0.2_Code.zip` | Selected unchanged scientific sources, package helpers and bounded offline startup | `QPathformer_v0.2_Code.seal.json` |

The packages omit datasets, checkpoints, installed environments and complete operational archives. Code startup checks imports, in-memory predictions, an explicit invariant, CLI help and a small CPU text forward; it does not establish full reproduction or a clean-room installation. Verify each ZIP and seal before use. [Exact download sizes and SHA-256 values](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/f65722c17c54ff67dd018f5a299526d984fe9325/release_preparation/study-v0.2/revisions/draft_20261029_r4/PACKAGE_INDEX.json) identify this candidate.

### Rights and verification

releases.name: Q-Pathformer Study v0.1 — Local Benchmark and QPU Readiness
releases.body:
# Q-Pathformer Study v0.1 — Local Benchmark and QPU Readiness

**Study · Documentation · Code**

This release brings the completed v0.1 study into **Q-Pathformer Classical Research, repository edition v1.0**. It publishes an earlier study in the series; [study-v0.9.5](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/releases/tag/study-v0.9.5) remains the latest published study release.

The study explored input-dependent computation in two separate settings: small simulated quantum circuits and a classical text classifier with shared or content-routed adapters. “QPU readiness” means historical local circuit-translation and simulator checks, with no physical-QPU results or qualification for a currently selected device. The retained report uses the historical title “Local Benchmark and IBM Readiness”.

## Downloads

Download the three ZIPs and their matching `.seal.json` files from this release’s Assets section. Extract each ZIP once and open `START_HERE.md`. Seals record file integrity; they are not digital signatures. GitHub’s automatic source-code archives contain the tagged repository tree and are separate from these curated downloads.

| Package | What it contains |
| --- | --- |
| `QPathformer_v0.1_Study.zip` | Final report editions in PDF and Word, author metadata, edition changes and the adopted report-content license scope. |
| `QPathformer_v0.1_Documentation.zip` | Study overview, research guide, reproduction boundaries and source evidence. |
| `QPathformer_v0.1_Code.zip` | Selected circuit, classical neural-network, text-routing and offline-readiness code, with dependency details and a startup guide. |

## What the study found

The original v0.1 work includes a prototype capsule and a later full benchmark. The completed benchmark contains **45 synthetic training runs**, **ten AG News method results across five paired seeds**, and local readiness checks of **30 trained circuit checkpoints**. The two text methods reused the same warm-up within each seed. This study selection contains **no ETEL component**.

On the radial classification task, the scheduled circuit underperformed both a classical neural network given the same input information and the fixed four-layer circuit. The neural-network comparison matched available input information, not parameter count or computational cost. Shared and content-routed text adapters produced similar AG News results; uncertainty intervals for their paired difference included zero. These findings do not establish equivalence or quantum advantage.

The trained-checkpoint readiness audit used **3,686,400 simulated shots**, with **zero physical shots or hardware jobs**. [Study summary and limitations](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/study-v0.1/release_records/study-v0.1/packages/QPathformer_v0.1_Documentation/payload/project/release_notes/study-v0.1.md).

## Report and licensing

The final report edition preserves the study’s scientific content and results, updates presentation labels and author metadata, and explains the original report’s historical publication recommendation in an edition note.

Identified original report content and selected explanatory prose are licensed under **CC BY 4.0**. The selected Python files are source available under the unchanged **Q-Pathformer Platform License 1.0**. Anthony Siljeg adopted these scoped grants on **29 October 2026**. Earlier grants remain in force within their existing scopes, including already-licensed expression wherever reused. No dataset, dependency, model, architecture-document or whole-archive grant is implied.

[Exact adopted scopes and boundaries](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/study-v0.1/release_records/study-v0.1/README.md#licensed-content-and-boundaries) · [Adoption record](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/study-v0.1/release_records/study-v0.1/LICENSE_ADOPTION.json).

## Verification and reproduction

All three final ZIPs passed seal, inventory and fresh-extraction checks. The final Code package passed a new Windows startup check covering imports, CLI entry points, selected non-training tests and a local circuit compilation/matrix comparison. These package-startup checks did not run training, optimizer updates, shot sampling, dependency installation or QPU submission. They do not establish full study reproduction or fresh-install portability.

The separately retained benchmark archive totals approximately **9.18 GB of logical file content**, including its delivery manifest, according to the retained source-verification record. These downloads exclude raw datasets, trained checkpoints, installed environments and the full archive. Storage accounting is not a hardware or RAM minimum.

[Startup receipt](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/study-v0.1/release_records/study-v0.1/QPathformer_v0.1_Code.startup.json) · [Final package verification](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/study-v0.1/release_records/study-v0.1/FRESH_PACKAGE_VERIFICATION.json) · [Package identities](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/study-v0.1/release_records/study-v0.1/PACKAGE_INDEX.json) · [Retained archive verification](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/study-v0.1/release_records/study-v0.1/FROZEN_SOURCE_VERIFICATION.json).

Anthony Siljeg — Founder, Alnotrea Labs · Company affiliation: Alnotrea Pty Ltd · Q-Pathformer Initiative.

[Publication record](https://github.com/qpathformer/qpathformer-classical-research-v1.0/blob/7c05ea9712d4b21a3b16fd1258f2731972e344c2/provenance/publication-study-v0.1/PUBLICATION.json).
